title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: Continuous batching scheduler was exposing fairness and starvation issues under mixed-priority workloads. High-priority request streams occasionally starved low-priority background tenants for extended periods, and we observed timeouts triggered by long queueing delays in tail latencies. This PR tunes the scheduler to provide weighted fairness, aging-based starvation prevention, and more conservative per-request soft timeouts. What I changed (summary): implemented a priority-aware queue with configurable weights, added an aging multiplier so requests increase effective priority the longer they wait, tightened the enqueue/dequeue accounting to prevent priority inversion when dynamic batching occurs, and introduced a new per-request soft-timeout advisory (default 120s) that surfaces to the runtime for graceful cancellation and KV cache reclamation. Also added metrics and dashboards for queue-depth-by-priority, average-age, and starved-request-count, plus integration tests and perf canary scenarios. Behavioral changes and knobs: default scheduler now uses weights {high: 5, default: 3, low: 1} (configurable via scheduler.weights). Aging increases effective weight by +1 per 100ms wait up to a cap of +10. New config scheduler.soft_request_timeout_ms defaults to 120000 and is advisory - long-running model execution still completes but the runtime will proactively reclaim KV cache buffers for timed-out requests to reduce OOM risk. Benchmarks: micro-benchmarks run on perf-canary (A100s, mixed 3:1 ratio high:low QPS, 512 token average length) show overall throughput +6% for default-weighted workloads and p95 latency reduced by ~12% for low-priority requests under contention. No regression in high-priority p50/p95. Tail latency improved due to aging preventing long queue waits. Compatibility and rollout: change is backward compatible; configs added to yaml but have defaults. Rollout plan: staged rollout on Dedicated fleets -> perf canary -> gradual host rollout with metric gating (starved_request_count decrease, p95 tail improvement). Tests and verification: unit tests for queue ordering and aging, integration test that reproduces prior-starvation scenario, perf canary with synthetic mixed workloads. CI flake fixed by increasing test timeout in e2e. Checklist: [x] Unit tests [x] Integration tests [x] Perf canary [x] README and config docs updated [x] Metrics/dashboards added. Notes for operators: watch metrics "scheduler.queue_depth_by_priority", "scheduler.average_age_ms", and "scheduler.starved_requests". If you see increased cancellations because soft_request_timeout_ms is too aggressive, raise the value. For large-sequence workloads consider lowering scheduler.weights.high to reduce head-of-line blocking for default requests. References: related PRs pr-41213, pr-45021; Linear ENG-8742; support ticket SUP-4122.
